flags.description: Chef mode: the Settings switch (Steps section) for short steps written on the device, shown in the reading view and cook mode.

The free tier: 50 recipes (20 with oneCookbook off), a one-time unlock for unlimited, the Settings row to buy or restore it and the Recipes count. Off until the store products exist. Ignored while proUnlock is on.

A recipe picked from the page's text by the on-device model when the page has no JSON-LD or microdata recipe: every line kept is checked to be on the page, and the reading view says so. Needs ML Kit's Prompt API on Android (fewer phones than Chef mode: on Samsung only the S26, Z Fold7/8, Z Flip8 and TriFold) or Apple Intelligence on iOS; other phones and unsupported languages behave as before.

Typed decisions by the on-device model where the rules give up: whether a close pantry name is the same ingredient (Have/Buy), and the aisle of an item the keyword table puts in Other. Only a definite answer given twice with high confidence acts. Needs the same model as llmExtraction (Prompt API or Apple Intelligence); other phones and unsupported languages behave as before. Count brackets stay as written unless aiCountBrackets is on too.

With aiDecisions on, also asks the model whether a count's bracket is the total or each item's, and scales the line by its answer. Off, those lines scale as without the model. Kept to re-measure: the #105 evaluation found it confidently wrong on 4 of 22.

Reddit posts: a reddit.com or redd.it link (a /s/ share link is followed first) is read from the post's .json listing: the post body, else a transcription in the comments, else the post's photo and title with a note that no recipe text was found. Off, Reddit links go through the blog parsers like any page.

Read the photo: on a Reddit post with no recipe text, a button reads the post's photo (each picture of a gallery, in order) with on-device text recognition (ML Kit's bundled Latin model on Android, Vision on iOS). The lines are sorted by the Reddit splitter into the recipe editor for the cook to check (unsure lines are marked); nothing is saved without that. When nothing sorts, the editor opens with the title, photo and any lines read. Also Scan a recipe (#226): the cook's own photos, taken, picked or shared in, read the same way and saved as a typed-in recipe.

Running cook-mode timers outside the app: on Android an ongoing notification counting down to the saved deadline (a Live Update on Android 16), on iOS a Live Activity on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island. A tap opens the recipe in cook mode. Off, only the time's-up alert remains.

Home-screen widgets: Tonight (today's planned meals; a tap opens the Week) and Groceries (what's left to buy; a tap opens Groceries). They refresh when the plan or the list changes. Off, a widget already placed shows only the app's name.

Print or save as PDF: the recipe screen's menu prints the recipe as shown (scaled and converted, with its photo if cached, the note last) through the system print dialog, which can also save a PDF; a list's menu makes the whole list a cookbook PDF (a title page, contents, each recipe on its own page) for the share sheet.

Text shared into the app (a note, an email, a message): when it splits into a recipe (the Reddit splitter, in the text's language) it opens in the recipe editor for the cook to check, even with a link in it; text that doesn't split and isn't a bulleted list opens the editor with every line as a step. Nothing is saved unchecked. Off, shared text imports its link or offers its lines as a list, as before.

Use it up: a pantry item in stock that expires today or tomorrow (the expiry reminder's window) shows how many saved recipes (in at least one list) use it, matched by name as What I need matches; tapping that, or the expiry reminder, opens a sheet of those recipes, each with one tap to plan it today or on the use-by day. Off, the Pantry rows and the reminder are as before.

One cookbook: every recipe stays until the cook deletes it (the old clean-up of recipes in no list past 50 is gone), the free tier's limit is 50 and a new recipe at the limit is opened but not saved, under the quiet Not saved bar with Unlock (nothing old is removed to make room), and Recipes shows a strip of views (Not in a list, Cooked, Typed by you) followed by the lists, in place of the filter pills. Home's Recently viewed gains See all. Off, the app is as before: the clean-up of 50, the free tier's swap at 20, the filter pills.

Ask an AI: Home's fourth tile opens a sheet that copies or shares a prompt for any chat app (what to cook; What can I make from the pantry, items to use up first; Plan my week from favourites and recently cooked), and the recipe screen's menu gains Change this recipe (the recipe as schema.org JSON plus the cook's request). Every prompt asks for schema.org Recipe JSON in a json block, with the servings and the units from Settings, in the UI language; the answer comes back as shared text. No AI runs in the app. Off, neither entry is shown.

Meal-plan import: shared text holding a week of recipes (the answer to Ask an AI's Plan my week, one JSON array of schema.org Recipes, each with a day) opens a review instead of the single-recipe editor: the recipes with their days, each ticked, kept as from a chat and planned on its day in Week. Nothing is saved before Save; the free limit says how many fit. Off, the first recipe opens the editor as before.

Recipe versions: JSON shared in whose isBasedOn names a recipe in the library (its link, as Change this recipe wrote it) is saved as a version of it, linked by the original's uid. The version shows Based on the original (a tap opens it) and the original lists its versions. Off, the link is neither saved nor shown, and the recipe is a plain chat recipe.

Week's menu has one item, Shop for this week, which opens What I need for the week shown (To buy and In your pantry, Add to groceries adds To buy once). Off, the menu has the two items it had: What I need and Add this week's ingredients.

Reorder lists: a long press on a list's cover on the Lists screen lifts it to be dragged into place (and, for TalkBack or VoiceOver, Move earlier / Move later actions); the order is stored and used wherever lists are shown (Lists, the save-to-list sheet, Recipes) and carried by export and import. Off, lists are in the seeded-first order of before and cannot be moved.

Home's Today card: when nothing is being cooked, today's earliest planned meal not yet cooked (in the meal types' order) with Start cooking, the rest of today's meals on a line under it; a recipe cooked today (a cooking entry dated today, or a finished run) drops off, and so does a meal whose window has passed (breakfast 11:00, lunch 15:00), and with nothing left there is no card. Off, Home always shows the most recent recipe under Continue cooking, as before.

A Select all / Clear all row at the top of both pantry checklists: Done shopping's put-away sheet and Update the pantry after cooking. A tri-state checkbox that ticks or unticks every row; the sheets' own button still does all the writing. Shown only with two or more tickable rows. Off, the sheets are as before.

Recipes: quick filter chips under search (30 min or less, Not cooked yet, Uses what's in my pantry) that combine with each other, the search and the sort; the pantry chip shows how many of a recipe's ingredients you have on each row it keeps. Off, Recipes has no chips.
Recipes: a toggle beside the sort between the tidy rows and a photo grid (title under each photo, the bookmark kept); the choice is remembered. Off, Recipes is the rows.

A long press on a recipe row (Recipes, a view, a list) opens a menu: Add to list, Add to plan, Share, Delete, and in a list Remove from this list. Off, a row only opens its recipe (swipe to delete stays).

Select several recipes in Recipes, a view or a list (a Select action, or Select in the long-press menu): add them to a list, take them off this list, or delete them with one confirmation and one Undo. Off, no Select action or menu entry.

Import from Paprika: Settings, Your recipes gains a row that reads a Paprika export (.paprikarecipes, a zip of gzipped JSON recipes) into the library. Each recipe is kept as the cook's own version (never refreshed from its link) with its picture stored on the phone, nothing here is replaced or deleted, the free limit says how many were left out, and a switch (on) files recipes in lists by their Paprika categories. Off, the row is not shown.

Import from Recipe Keeper: Settings, Your recipes gains a row that reads a Recipe Keeper export (the .zip with recipes.html and its images folder) into the library, the same way as the Paprika import: each recipe is the cook's own version with its first picture stored on the phone, nothing is replaced or deleted, the free limit says how many were left out, and the switch files recipes in lists by their courses, categories and collections. Off, the row is not shown.

Import from Mealie: Settings, Your recipes gains a row that reads a Mealie export (the bulk export's zip of recipes/<slug>/<slug>.json, one recipe's Download zip with its .webp, or a bare .json) into the library. Each recipe is kept as the cook's own version (never refreshed from its link) with its picture stored on the phone, nothing here is replaced or deleted, the free limit says how many were left out, and a switch (on) files recipes in lists by their Mealie categories and tags. Off, the row is not shown.

A designed image for a recipe with no photo, or whose photo fails to load: the title's first letter on a small thumbnail, the recipe's first ingredient names in italic on a cover, Home's card and the reading view's banner, on one of five warm tints chosen by the recipe's uid. Lists covers show those recipes' images in the mosaic when no recipe in the list has a photo. Off, the blank tile and band as before.

Skip tonight: a planned meal's long-press menu on Week, and today's planned meals, gain Skip, which asks: push the rest of the week back a day (this meal and every later planned meal, meal types kept), move this meal to the next day with no meal of its type, or remove it from the plan. One undo restores exactly what was there. Off, Week offers Move and Remove only.

Evening-before reminder: a notification at the cook's time (19:00 by default, Settings > Week) naming tomorrow's planned meals and quoting any step to start ahead of time (marinate, soak, thaw, chill for hours, rise overnight, found by a word table in the recipe's own language); a tap opens the first recipe on the Week tab. An optional afternoon "Tonight" reminder (off by default). Off, neither is scheduled and Settings has no Week section.

Fresh food (#396): Shop for this week splits To buy into Buy now and Buy later in the week (a perishable ingredient, matched in the recipe's language's perishables table, whose every planned meal is 3 or more days from today), each later line saying the day it is for, with its own Add to groceries; the meal-plan review and the Week's meal rows gain a quiet note when a perishable meal is planned later than its group keeps from the plan's first day ('keeps about 1-2 days once bought: cook it earlier?'), with a one-tap swap with the earliest day that fits. Nothing moves unless the cook taps. Off, To buy is one list and there is no note.

Recipe tags (#422): in Groceries and in Shop for this week, the recipe a line is for is a small rounded tag tinted with the paprika wash and a book glyph ("Mushroom omelette · Thu" when planned), apart from the line's amount and note; up to three show, then the first two and "+N". A tap opens the recipe (at the planned servings when it came from the plan), on the current tab. A typed or shared-list line has no tag. Off, the recipes are the muted line under the row as before.

Ask an AI's Plan my week with choices: the cook's meal types as chips (Dinner ticked, the last choice remembered), a start day, and a source: new recipes, from my recipes (the library or one list, named by link) or a mix. The reader takes each recipe's meal, an object naming a saved recipe by its link is planned from the library, and the review shows and changes day and meal. Off, the sheet and the review are as before: a week of dinners, new recipes.

Pro (#413): unlimited recipes for everyone (the free tier's limit never applies, whatever freeTier says), and the one-time unlock of #107 re-pointed at Pro, which holds the Week planning extras: fresh food's Buy later and its 'cook it earlier?' swap, the evening and Tonight reminders, Skip, and Plan my week's choices. Each shows a quiet Pro badge and opens the Pro screen until unlocked; nothing already saved or switched on is taken away. Off, the app is as before: freeTier decides the limit and every extra is free.

Library first (#375): the Recipes tab opens the library, not Home. The Today / Continue cooking card sits compact above search while there is something to cook, the library's + opens an Add a recipe sheet (Paste a link, Scan a recipe, Type a recipe, Ask an AI), the Settings gear sits beside the Recipes title, and an empty library shows the four ways in as tiles. Needs oneCookbook (its views strip carries the Lists card): with that off the tab keeps opening Home. Off, the Recipes tab opens Home as before.

Settings links (#412): the Plan tab's menu gains "Plan settings" (Settings' Plan section, its reminders; only while that section shows, with eveningReminders) and the Pantry's "Pantry settings" (its expiry reminders), each opening that section's page on the tab's own stack, so Back returns to the tab. Groceries has no section, so no link. Off, Settings is reached only from the gear beside the Recipes title.

Recipe tips (#432): a page's schema.org HowToTip entries (kingarthurbaking.com lists them after the method) are kept apart from the steps as the recipe's tips, shown as written below the method under a quiet Tips heading, unnumbered, and left out of cook mode. Off, a newly parsed recipe's tips are its last steps, as before; tips already stored still show.

Step photos (#433): a step the source gives photos for (JSON-LD HowToStep.image, as Cookist does, its "(1)" markers left as written) shows a small thumbnail beside its text in the reading view, badged with its number (a stack with +1 for two or more), and a smaller one in cook mode (the current step's beside its timer, or beside its text when it has none); a tap opens a full-screen viewer that swipes through every step photo with its step's text. The photos are parsed, stored and exported whether it is on or not. Off, the screens are as before.

Recipes written inside an article: on a page with no JSON-LD or microdata recipe, each list in the article whose items are mostly amounts (at least 3, more than half), with its method in paragraphs or an ordered list up to the next heading, is a recipe (at most 6, named by the heading above it). One opens the editor (Check the recipe) straight away in the import's place, filled in as written; several open a chooser first. The same past Cloudflare's check in the clip view. Saved only on Save, as a clip under the page's link (a later recipe adds pith_recipe=<n>). Never from prose alone, never saved unchecked. Off, such a page ends at No recipe found as before.

Close the Today card (#448): the Today card (#402) at the top of Recipes (or Home) gains a small close button that hides it for the rest of the day (the local date is kept in settings, today_card_dismissed_day; it returns the next day), and Settings' Plan section a switch, Show today's meal (show_today_card, on by default), that hides it altogether. The mid-cook Continue cooking card is never closable and ignores both. Off, no close button and no switch: the card is as before.

The top of Recipes redesigned (#449, design B; with libraryFirst): the title row is Recipes, the + and a ⋮ menu holding Select and Settings (no gear, no Select button); the views are one segmented shelf of five cells (Lists, Not in a list, Cooked, Typed by you, From a chat) above search, each an icon, its count and its name; the three quick filters move into a sheet behind a filter button at the end of the search field, badged with how many are on, and those on show under search as removable pills with Clear; selecting gains Select all. Off, the top is as before.

A quiet pantry note on the Plan (#456): under each planned recipe from today on, one muted line naming the ingredients the pantry hasn't got, by name only (PantryMatch, as #378's "Uses what's in my pantry"; presence only, never "enough"): "Not in your pantry: tahini, sumac", up to three names, past that two and "and N more". None for a note, when every nameable line is had, or when the pantry has nothing in the recipe's language. No icon, colour, dialog or snackbar, and nothing in the add flow. Off, the Plan is as before.
